solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Uranium inside carried out — lots thus sold (9)

indicatorNotes.inside: 'inside' is used literally: the uranium symbol is placed within the other word

blocks.note: to action something is to carry it out
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

annotation.surface: A report on a nuclear consignment disposed of in bulk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lots' looks like 'a great many', but it means the numbered items at a sale, so the definition describes how they are sold.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: sale-room lots go under the hammer one by one to the highest bidder.

entries.clue: Arsenic very good cold in jelly (5)

blocks.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
pi, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good
C = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A poisoner's recipe: arsenic set in a cold jelly.
annotation.walkthrough: PI for 'very good' (pious) is a crossword convention worth learning.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain hypernym: a savoury jelly made from meat or fish stock.

entries.clue: Agree to welcome in New Year with dope smoker (7,3)

indicatorNotes.to welcome in: a host welcomes a guest in, so CHIME takes N inside

blocks.note: to chime with something is to agree with it

annotation.surface: Seeing in the New Year with a cannabis user.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smoker' looks like the dope user, but it is the thing on the roof that the smoke comes out of.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful sense: the pipe on top of a chimney gives out smoke, so it is jokingly a smoker.

entries.clue: Redeveloped Butlin’s covers area in Eurasian city (8)

indicatorNotes.Redeveloped: a redeveloped site is rebuilt in a new layout, so the letters of BUTLINS are rearranged
indicatorNotes.covers: to cover is to spread over, so the rebuilt letters sit around A

annotation.surface: A British holiday camp gets a makeover and spreads over a site in some city.
annotation.walkthrough: Butlin's is a chain of British seaside holiday camps, which is why 'redeveloped' reads so naturally.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the city straddles the Bosporus, so it lies partly in Europe and partly in Asia.

entries.clue: Composition for nine performing in drag? (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' is used literally: one thing placed within another, so ON goes inside NET

blocks.note: a drag is a net pulled along a river bed or sea floor
a performer on stage is on

annotation.surface: A piece of music written for nine drag artists.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Performing in drag' pictures a drag act, but drag is the fishing net.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical term: a piece written for nine players, as a quartet is for four.

entries.clue: Soldier to turn traitor — twice (6,3)

blocks.note: to desert is to abandon your side
the second go at 'turn traitor': to rat on someone

annotation.surface: A soldier who goes over to the enemy twice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twice' asks for two words for turning traitor.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division in the North African campaign of the Second World War.

entries.clue: Plumbing plans for castles in Spain? (4,6)

annotation.definition: Plumbing plans for castles in Spain?

blocks.note: a plumber's plans would be about pipes
castles in Spain are impossible daydreams

annotation.surface: A plumber drawing up schemes for Spanish castles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Castles in Spain' is an old phrase for unrealistic hopes, which is the plain meaning; the plumbing gives the literal pipe reading.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: hopes that can never come true, like castles in Spain, read literally as a plumber's dreams.

entries.clue: Under pressure, consume carbon-rich fuel (4)

indicatorNotes.Under: in a down clue, what is under something is written below it, so EAT goes under P

annotation.surface: Under stress, someone burns a carbon-heavy fuel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Under pressure' reads as a set phrase meaning stressed, but in a down clue it places one word below the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: partly decayed plant matter, cut from bogs and burned as fuel.

entries.clue: Support for pirate in fix on stage? (3,3)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one thing on another sits on top of it, so PEG comes above LEG

blocks.note: to peg something is to fix it in place
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

annotation.surface: An actor playing a pirate in a tight spot on stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In fix on stage' reads as a theatrical crisis, but fix and stage are separate synonyms.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the stock pirate stands on a wooden leg in place of a lost limb.

entries.clue: Drops book Waugh wrote? (7,3,4)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Drops' is plural; the answer is read as a noun phrase for a long drop, a downfall.
annotation.surface: A question about which book of Waugh's someone put down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drops' looks like a verb; it is taken as a noun for a slide from greatness.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a slide from greatness, as in Gibbon's Roman history, and the title of Evelyn Waugh's first novel.

entries.clue: Festival’s nutty Sauternes indeed drawing in daughter (6,6)

indicatorNotes.nutty: nutty means crazy, so the letters of SAUTERNES go mad
indicatorNotes.drawing in: to draw something in is to pull it inside, so D is pulled in between the pieces

blocks.note: ay is an old word for yes, indeed

annotation.surface: A festival where the sweet wine has a nutty taste and draws the daughter in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nutty' looks like a tasting note for the wine, which is a sweet white from Bordeaux, but it tells its letters to go mad.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the day Christians celebrate the Resurrection is one of the church's chief festivals.

entries.clue: Lassitude sadly besetting island in Middle East (7)

indicatorNotes.besetting: to beset is to surround on all sides, as enemies beset a town, so ALAS surrounds I
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' is used literally: the result is placed within ME

blocks.note: alas is a cry of sadness

annotation.surface: Listlessness sadly afflicting an island in the Middle East.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' looks like an adverb colouring the lassitude, but it stands for the sigh itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a vague feeling of weariness and unease.

entries.clue: Butter up witnesses drinking wicked French port (10)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, a word sent up is read from the bottom, so RAM becomes MAR
indicatorNotes.drinking: a drinker takes liquid in, so SEES takes ILL inside

blocks.note: a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter
ill can mean evil or wicked

annotation.surface: Flattering witnesses who are drinking a nasty French wine at a port.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Butter up' looks like a phrase for flattery, but a butter is one who butts.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: France's chief Mediterranean port.

entries.clue: Opt for a quiet beer, imbibing nothing? (7)

indicatorNotes.imbibing: to imbibe is to drink in, so PINT takes O inside

annotation.surface: Choosing a quiet pint, but one with nothing in it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nothing' looks like the beer being alcohol-free, but it is the round zero shape.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to choose someone for a post or task.

entries.clue: Losing act somehow — feeling sentimental? Not for now (9)

indicatorNotes.somehow: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are arranged some other way

annotation.surface: A failing stage act that leaves someone wistful.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition says what kind of sentimental: longing not for the present but for the past.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: sentimental longing aimed at times gone by rather than now.

entries.clue: Salvation Army youngster leaves meal (5)

annotation.surface: A young Salvation Army member walks out of a meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' pretends to be the youngster walking out; it joins the two halves and hints that the meal is made of leaves.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a bowl of leaves and toppings can be served as a light meal on its own.

entries.clue: Cast aspersions on circle visibly embarrassed by sex (9)

blocks.note: a disc is a flat circle
it is an old euphemism for sex or sex appeal

annotation.surface: Smearing a social circle that blushes at talk of sex.
annotation.walkthrough: IT for sex (or sex appeal) is a crossword convention.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to damage someone's reputation by hinting at wrongdoing.

entries.clue: One about to be exhumed from unconsecrated ground in habit (6,6)

indicatorNotes.to be exhumed from: to exhume is to dig out of the earth, so one C is dug out of the word
indicatorNotes.ground: ground means crushed, so the remaining letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: c = circa, about; there are two Cs and only one goes

annotation.surface: A body due to be dug up from ground that was never blessed.
annotation.walkthrough: The graveyard picture hides the mechanics: 'about' is circa, 'one' says only one of the two Cs, and 'ground' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a habit so ingrained it feels instinctive, as if part of your nature.

entries.clue: What DPD and Evri bring over? (10)

annotation.definitionNote: 'over' is singular; an over in cricket is made up of six of these.

blocks.note: DPD and Evri are British parcel companies
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled at the batsman

annotation.surface: Asking what the parcel couriers bring round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bring over' reads as one phrase; split it and 'over' is the cricket term, six balls in a row from one bowler.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the parcels couriers drop off, and the six balls that make up a cricket over.

entries.clue: Divine king captured by enemy archer (8)

indicatorNotes.captured by: a captive is held in the captor's grip, so FOE holds R inside

annotation.surface: A godlike king taken prisoner by an enemy bowman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective for the king; it is the verb, to divine the future.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to predict the future by insight or magic.

entries.clue: Forgive me for what? (1,3,4,6)

blocks.note: a request to hear something again

annotation.surface: Someone asks forgiveness without knowing what they did.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase has two uses: an apology and a polite 'what did you say?'.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one idiom: an apology, and a polite request to repeat something.

entries.clue: Calm and painless death? (4-5)

blocks.note: going can mean dying, and a painless one is gentle

annotation.surface: Wishing for peace and a gentle end.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading: 'going' as a euphemism for dying.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a relaxed, placid temperament, and, read literally, a gentle departure from life.

entries.clue: About time to cut post-work allowance? Unjustified claim (10)

indicatorNotes.to cut: to cut into something is to make a gap in it, so RE and T go inside PENSION

blocks.note: a pension is paid after you stop work
re = about, as in a memo

annotation.surface: Talk of trimming pensions, dismissed as a baseless claim.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Post-work allowance' is a roundabout description of retirement pay, and the cut lands just after its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a claim to merit or status that is not justified.

entries.clue: Space in M&S to be reduced in department there? (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' is used literally: EN is placed within the letters of M&S

blocks.note: an en is a printer's space
to wear down is to be reduced by use

annotation.surface: Marks & Spencer shrinking its floor space.
annotation.walkthrough: M&S is Marks & Spencer, a British high-street clothing store. 'There' points back to it, so the definition is one of its departments.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Marks & Spencer sells clothes, and the men's section is one of its departments.

entries.clue: Long-faced Ishmael finally smashed — false idol (6,4)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so take the last letter of Ishmael
indicatorNotes.smashed: something smashed is broken into bits, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A gloomy Ishmael finally smashes a false idol.
annotation.walkthrough: The Bible theme fits the surface: Ishmael is a figure from Genesis, and the idol belongs to Exodus.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the idol the Israelites made and worshipped while Moses was on Mount Sinai.

entries.clue: At first, life is good in French city (6)

indicatorNotes.At first: at first means at the beginning, so take the first letter of life

annotation.surface: A remark that life is good in some French city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French city' looks like the definition, but French belongs to the wordplay and the city is Portuguese.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the capital of Portugal.

entries.clue: Sit comfortably with feathers on bench (6,4)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, one thing on another is attached after it, so DOWN follows SETTLE

blocks.note: a settle is a high-backed wooden bench

annotation.surface: Getting cosy on a bench with a feather cushion.
annotation.walkthrough: A settle is an old-fashioned wooden bench, often with a high back.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb: to make yourself comfortable in a seat.

entries.clue: Wandering tribesman friend to Pythias recalled (5)

indicatorNotes.recalled: recalled means called back, so the name is read backwards

blocks.note: Damon and Pythias, the loyal friends of Greek legend

annotation.surface: A roving tribesman remembered as the friend of Pythias.
annotation.walkthrough: Damon and Pythias were two friends from Greek legend, each ready to die for the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a member of a people that moves from place to place.

entries.clue: Doctor followed advice, discharging litres, and got damp (9)

indicatorNotes.discharging: to discharge is to let out, so L is let go from the word

blocks.note: to listen is to heed advice

annotation.surface: A doctor who took advice, passed fluids and ended up damp.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes 'discharging litres' sound like a symptom; it only drops a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: became slightly wet.

entries.clue: Month after rep cousin bungled — part in theatre (10,4)

indicatorNotes.after: after means following, so MARCH comes behind the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.bungled: something bungled is botched, so REP COUSIN is jumbled into a new order

annotation.surface: A cousin in repertory theatre fluffs a part after a month.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part in theatre' looks like an acting role; it is a part of the building. Rep is repertory theatre.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the arch that frames the stage opening in a traditional theatre.

entries.clue: Wise man brought back fuel allowance in the end (4)

indicatorNotes.brought back: something brought back returns the way it came, so GAS is read backwards
indicatorNotes.in the end: in the end means at the finish, so take the last letter of allowance

annotation.surface: A wise man restores the winter fuel allowance after all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fuel allowance' looks like one unit, a British winter heating payment, but it splits into two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a person of profound wisdom, such as a philosopher or revered elder.

entries.clue: Brother harbouring wonder about shared programs (8)

indicatorNotes.harbouring: to harbour is to shelter someone, so FRERE takes the other piece inside
indicatorNotes.about: about as in turned about, facing the other way, so AWE runs backwards

blocks.note: a frere is a brother or friar, from French frère

annotation.surface: A monk sheltering someone amazed by shared software.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brother' is a religious brother here, and the old word for one comes from the French.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: software given away free for anyone to copy and share.

entries.clue: Stealthy assassin strangling orc upset Scottish writer (1,1,6)

indicatorNotes.strangling: a strangler's hands go round the neck, so one word wraps round the other
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, something upset is turned upside down, so the whole is read from the bottom

blocks.note: a ninja is a Japanese covert assassin

annotation.surface: A ninja throttling a goblin, upsetting a Scottish novelist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' is placed last so it reads as the writer's mood, but in a down clue it turns the whole assembly upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Scottish doctor and novelist who wrote The Citadel.

entries.clue: One expects frustration — believer hiding achievement (9)

indicatorNotes.hiding: to hide something is to keep it inside, out of view, so DEIST keeps FEAT within

annotation.surface: A believer who expects to be let down keeps quiet about a success.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One expects frustration' reads as a sentence, but 'One' is the start of the definition: a person who expects it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a person who expects to lose, or to be thwarted, before even trying.

entries.clue: Book from Greater Manchester town is about a revolutionary group (12)

indicatorNotes.about: about in the sense of around, so IS goes round A
indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution is a turn round, so SET revolves into TES

annotation.surface: A book from Eccles about a group of revolutionaries.
annotation.walkthrough: Eccles is a town in Greater Manchester, famous for its currant cakes. 'Revolutionary' turns a word round rather than describing the group.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the wisdom books of the Old Testament, traditionally ascribed to Solomon.

entries.clue: Legal action applied to odd characters — those taken away? (9)

blocks.note: an odd person is a case

annotation.surface: A lawsuit against some eccentrics who are then removed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taken away' sounds like an arrest, but it means taken away on holiday.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: the luggage people take with them when they go away on a trip.

entries.clue: Reportedly observe shores adapted for marine life (9)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so take the word by its sound
indicatorNotes.adapted: something adapted is changed to suit, so SHORES is changed into a new order

annotation.surface: A report on coastlines adapted for sea creatures.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Adapted for marine life' reads as habitat planning, but 'adapted' only rearranges the word before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: small upright fish of the sea are one kind of marine life.

entries.clue: Cell soon prepared for military personnel (8)

indicatorNotes.prepared: something prepared is made ready by working it over, so the letters are put in a new order

annotation.surface: A cell is being readied for some army officers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cell' and 'prepared' read as a jail being readied; the two fodder words are only letters to reshuffle.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: senior army officers are military personnel.

entries.clue: Lead removed from gold for example, and the rest (2,2)

indicatorNotes.Lead removed from: the lead is the front runner, so the first letter comes off

blocks.note: gold is an example of a metal

annotation.surface: Refining metals: lead taken out of gold and everything else.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal, which fits the gold, but it means the leading letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latin abbreviation: et alii, and others, used at the end of lists.

entries.clue: Line to repeat involving Sumerian city’s valued works (10)

indicatorNotes.involving: to involve is literally to wrap in, so ITERATE wraps round UR

annotation.surface: Repeating a line about the treasured writings of an ancient city.
annotation.walkthrough: Ur, in modern Iraq, is the crossword's standard ancient city. The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: written works valued for their artistic merit.

entries.clue: German woman detective on Yard team investigating deception (5,5)

blocks.note: a quad is a quadrangle, an enclosed yard

annotation.surface: A German policewoman working with Scotland Yard on a fraud case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Yard' looks like Scotland Yard, the London police headquarters, which suits the surface, but it is an enclosed courtyard.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the police unit that handles cheating and swindling cases.

entries.clue: Divine creature in a northern set (5)

blocks.note: to gel is to set, like jelly

annotation.surface: A heavenly being among a set of northerners.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a group, which suits the picture, but it is the verb, what jelly does.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a messenger of God in Christian, Jewish and Islamic belief.

entries.clue: English, rich, to keep on being prudent (10)

indicatorNotes.to keep: to keep something is to hold on to it, so COMICAL holds ON inside

blocks.note: rich can mean highly amusing, as in 'that's rich'

annotation.surface: A rich Englishman who keeps on being careful with money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rich' looks like wealth, which fits being prudent, but it means funny.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: careful with money and avoiding waste.

entries.clue: Nervous desire that’s dismissed with a taunt (3,2,4)

indicatorNotes.that’s dismissed: to dismiss is to send away, so the W for 'with' is sent out of WILL

blocks.note: will is desire, as in 'against my will'

annotation.surface: An anxious wish brushed off with a jeer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a link, but it is the abbreviation that gets dismissed.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: uneasy and awkward, the opposite of relaxed.

entries.clue: Sword beginning to trouble old German statesman (6)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning is the start, so take the first letter of trouble

blocks.note: brand is a poetic word for a sword

annotation.surface: A sword starting trouble for a former German leader.
annotation.walkthrough: Brand for sword is old poetic usage worth knowing.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Willy Brandt was West German chancellor from 1969 to 1974.

entries.clue: Controversial diarist: Mister X? (8)

annotation.surface: A newspaper-style tag hiding the name of a notorious diarist behind 'Mister X'.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mister X' reads as an anonymous man; the letter is the mark, and the order is swapped. The diarist was a British Labour cabinet minister.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Richard Crossman's cabinet diaries caused a legal row when published in the 1970s.

entries.clue: Very exciting men chat with Mike (8)

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
a mike or mic is a microphone

annotation.surface: Men talking into a microphone, thrilled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mike' looks like a name, or the M of the radio alphabet; here it is the microphone.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose, informal sense: intensely thrilling.

entries.clue: Slow Greek racing driver Niki pulled up (7)

indicatorNotes.pulled up: in a down clue, a word pulled up is read from the bottom, so LAUDA is turned round

blocks.note: Niki Lauda, Formula One world champion

annotation.surface: A Greek driver is too slow and Niki Lauda pulls up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pulled up' is what a racing driver does when he stops, but here it turns the surname upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: happening slowly, by degrees.

entries.clue: Film Grand National winner set to make return, holding form (4,1,3,6)

indicatorNotes.to make return: to return is to go back the way you came, so the two words are read backwards
indicatorNotes.holding: to hold is to keep inside, so the reversed letters hold FORM

blocks.note: Red Rum won Britain's Grand National horse race three times
to set something down is to lay it; laid

annotation.surface: A racehorse set for a comeback, holding its form.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word of the surface is racing talk, 'form' included, so the film hides well. The horse's name famously reads as a word backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Alfred Hitchcock's 1954 thriller, adapted from a stage play.

entries.clue: An exceptional victory having shunned local court (6)

indicatorNotes.having shunned: to shun is to avoid, so the victory steers clear of PH

blocks.note: a triumph is an outstanding victory
a local is a pub, a public house (PH); removed

annotation.surface: An outstanding win for someone who avoided the local court.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Local court' reads as a magistrates' court; split it, and a local is the neighbourhood pub.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an open central court or hall in a building.

entries.clue: Military camp declared strength in column coming up (10)

indicatorNotes.declared: to declare is to say out loud, so MIGHT is heard as MITE

blocks.note: a stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp

annotation.surface: An army camp shows its might in a parade column.
annotation.walkthrough: The cave column that grows up from the floor is this one; the one that hangs down has a C. 'Coming up' is the fair way to tell them apart.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a mineral column rising from the floor of a cave.

entries.clue: Immediately visiting top tourist attraction? (2,5,5)

blocks.note: a tourist attraction is a sight, and the top one is the first

annotation.surface: A tourist heads straight for the biggest attraction.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading, where a tourist attraction is a sight and you are at the top one.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: straight away, on first seeing something, and literally standing at the number-one sight.

entries.clue: This writer shows contentment in supporting structure (1-4)

blocks.note: to beam is to smile broadly

annotation.surface: The setter says they are happy in their support.
annotation.walkthrough: The girder is named for its cross-section, which is shaped like the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a steel girder used to hold up floors and roofs.

entries.clue: Upstanding character exiting master class (5)

indicatorNotes.exiting: to exit is to leave, so the I goes out of GENIUS

blocks.note: a genius is a master of an art
I is the letter that stands upright; removed

annotation.surface: An honest person walks out of a masterclass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding character' looks like a moral person, but it is the upright letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a class of related things, especially in biological classification.

entries.clue: Junkie husband absent from show (4)

indicatorNotes.absent from: to be absent is to be missing, so H is missing from the word

blocks.note: to usher someone in is to show them in

annotation.surface: An addict's husband skips a show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a noun, a performance; it is the verb, as in show someone to their seat.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang: someone who takes illegal drugs, an addict.

entries.clue: Exploit what bonsai growers do (5)

blocks.note: as a noun: a daring feat

annotation.surface: A question about what bonsai growers get up to.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' looks like a verb, to take advantage of; it is the noun, a feat.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a daring feat, and to stop something growing to full size, as bonsai growers do to trees.

entries.clue: Bring back means of controlling condition (9)

annotation.surface: Reintroducing a way of keeping a condition under control.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Means of controlling' sounds abstract, but it is the strap a rider holds.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to restore something to a former position or use.

entries.clue: Maybe person in Black Sea abroad capturing old vessel (7)

indicatorNotes.capturing: a captor holds a prisoner inside, so MER holds O and URN

annotation.surface: Someone on the Black Sea, far from home, seizing an ancient ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Black Sea' is split: Black belongs to the definition, someone dressed in black. 'Maybe' says not everyone in black is at a funeral.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: people at a funeral traditionally wear black.

entries.clue: Irreverent sort — disturbed lamb, sheep and ram, initially (10)

indicatorNotes.disturbed: something disturbed is thrown out of order, so the letters are stirred up
indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of ram

annotation.surface: Someone irreverent upsets a whole flock.
annotation.walkthrough: The farmyard words are all fodder; 'and' joins them.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: someone who speaks irreverently about sacred things.

entries.clue: Greek dramatist sheds tear for men and furious women (9)

indicatorNotes.sheds: to shed something is to cast it off, as a tree sheds leaves, so RIP is dropped
indicatorNotes.for: for in the sense 'in exchange for', so MEN takes RIP's place

blocks.note: a tear is a rip; removed

annotation.surface: A Greek playwright weeps for men and angry women.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sheds tear' looks like crying, but a tear here rhymes with 'bear': a rip.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: the Furies, avenging goddesses of Greek myth, are literally furious women.
